name: The Vertical City
description: Considered the foundational blockbuster of the neural-feed era, this Vantablack Media production cast the viewer as Dara Okonkwo-Petrov, a Spire security architect uncovering a terrorist network embedded in M88's vertical transit infrastructure. The neural-capture technology was primitive by later standards — emotional cues were blunt, physical sensations inconsistent — but the sheer ambition of placing viewers in a Tier 5 body looking down at the city below created a cultural rupture. It remains the highest-grossing film in M88 history adjusted for currency fluctuation.
cultural_impact: The Vertical City made neural-feed entertainment aspirational for Tier 2 audiences and drove mass adoption of consumer BCI hardware, effectively building Vantablack Media's distribution monopoly.
story_hooks: The original neural-capture performer for Dara Okonkwo-Petrov has written a memoir alleging the production team recorded and retained her full sensory profile without consent.
An unedited neural-capture session from the film's production contains footage of an actual corporate meeting that was accidentally recorded during a set visit.
A Tier 1 archivist has assembled a cut of the film using only the scenes depicting Shelf characters, creating an entirely different story about the same events.
